Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: eCRVS integrated with national ID system (Ministry Interior); generates unique national ID numbers real-time.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a second corroborating source. World Bank (2024) confirms the eCRVS system generates unique national ID numbers in real time and that a formal interoperability MOU between the Ministry of Health, Ministry of Interior and Ministry of Communications & Digital Economy was only signed 22 March 2024, i.e. integration exists but is recent and not yet universal — consistent with 'Partially integrated' (4).

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Mass registration 1.17M/ ~2.7M pop =43% verified eBC (household survey March 2023); prior paper 59%; 50-69%.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Evidence is genuinely mixed. World Bank (2024) says the 2022-23 mass campaign registered 1.17m people, which it calls 'more than half the population' but which is arithmetically closer to 43-47% of ~2.5-2.7m residents; UNICEF (2020, citing MICS 2018) puts overall birth registration completeness at 58% (up from 53% in 2010), though only 32% of under-5s held an actual certificate. Depending on which denominator is used the true figure could sit in either the 20-49% or 50-69% band. Kept at 50-69% but flagged for human review given the conflicting percentages across sources; no fresher (2024-2026) national survey was found to resolve this.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital electoral register?
Comments: Partial digitalisation ahead 2026 polls: GIS polling stations, digital results transmission planned; voter registration ongoing.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source only described a forthcoming GIS overlay of polling stations and undecided plans for digital results transmission, which does not support even 'Under development'. Fresh, corroborating evidence shows the IEC already operates a mature, continuously-updated nationwide biometric voter register with fingerprint and photo capture (International IDEA database); Electoral Services International confirms this is its fourth biometric voter registration (BVR) contract with the IEC over two decades, with the current exercise (March-October 2026) updating the existing 2021 voter roll ahead of the December 2026 presidential election (ESI; Dubawa, 2026). Revised up to 'Fully deployed nationwide' (5).

Definition: What proportion of the intended beneficiaries does the register cover?
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. World Bank blog (April 2024) states the Gambia Social Registry (GamSR) covers 203,022 households across 40 of 43 districts, representing 70% of the national population, matching the cited figure and the 70-89% band exactly. Only one primary source was found, so treat as confirmed-but-single-sourced.

Definition: Does the government maintain one or more tax registers?
Comments: Gambia Revenue Authority (GRA) has taxpayer register; online TIN application form.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: 'Fully deployed nationwide' is not supported. In June 2026 GRA's own Commissioner General stated domestic tax administration 'is largely manual' and that the new Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS), which will enable e-registration, e-filing and e-payment, is only now being sensitised to taxpayers ahead of a still-pending nationwide rollout under the World Bank-funded PAMP programme. Customs (ASYCUDA World) and basic TIN/online tax calculators are already digital, so the register is neither absent nor fully deployed; revised down to 'Partially deployed' (4).
